Type erasure works today but is fragile — adding any runtime sibling (e.g. a const array next to the type) breaks the client import. Discovered when planning F22 audit renderer that wanted both AuditMeta and KNOWN_AUDIT_ACTIONS from packages/db/src/audit.ts (which has import 'server-only').

Redundant exhaustiveness guards inside nested switch statements actively fail tsc. After the inner switch covers all sub-values, TS narrows the discriminated field to never, then  triggers 'Property reason does not exist on type never' AND 'Type any not assignable to never'. Trust the outer-switch's exhaustive default; don't double-guard.

Account sub-pages plan reverses the 2026-05-26 'no notification preference toggles until real need surfaces' decision; new plan adds 2 binary email-gating toggles + wires email sends in messages/community services, since toggle UI without wire-up is vapor.

packages/services/* is pure business logic — email sends MUST live at the operation/app layer (apps/web/src/server/operations/* or apps/web/src/lib/cron/*), never inside services. Pattern: service call returns, op handler does follow-up read + email send + try/catch logging.
Generic sendNotificationEmail({title, body, ctaLabel, ctaUrl}) at packages/email/src/templates.tsx:125 handles most transactional sends — check for it before proposing new React Email template files.

Replit Agent auto-commits intercept mlabs-code mid-task on this workspace. Manifested as: my service-file edits + my staged test files were swallowed into an auto-named 'Published your App' + 'Add tests...' commit pair between my git add and git commit; my own commit then aborted with 'nothing to commit'. Functional impact: zero. Hygiene impact: task 5 lacks a clean feat(services) commit by Claude. Don't rebase-fight — document and move on.

businesses.tier was a manual admin lever that drifted from the subscription that paid for it because membership_plan had no tier column. The plan-tier-derivation work makes membership_plan declare placement and the subscription service propagates the tier to businesses on every mutation. Kept tier1/tier2/tier3 internal codes; relabel only in UI via TIER_LABELS map exported from @aira/validators.

Subscription-service mutations (createSubscription, updateSubscription, deleteSubscription, rolloverExpiredSubscriptions) must be wrapped in db.transaction(...) once they trigger downstream side-effects like businesses.tier recompute. Bare INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with an out-of-band recompute can race against concurrent admins. neon-serverless WS Pool gives a real BEGIN/COMMIT; test mocks invoke transaction(cb) by calling cb(mockDb).

When a Zod schema is .strict() and a field is removed from it, sending the field yields a Zod 'unrecognized key' 400 error at the request boundary — that's the only feedback signal needed. Adding a separate warn-log inside the handler is dead code (the request never reaches it).

Permission union widened from user|admin to user|admin|super_admin in @aira/api. Hierarchy: super_admin >= admin >= user. defineOperation gates via hasPermission() so existing permission:"admin" ops accept super_admin callers (no regression). The role-collapse in operations/index.ts and getCallerContext() must be removed in lockstep so OperationSession.user.role carries the real DB role. Reason: requireSuperAdmin() existed in auth/server.ts since W8 but had zero callers because the api package had no way to enforce it declaratively. Adding the second axis to Permission (privilege level) — but NOT generalizing to a flag matrix; permission.ts comment about 'don't pre-build it' still applies.

When widening @aira/api's Permission union, the operation-layer admin freshness gate at packages/api/src/operation.ts:170-176 needs to widen in lockstep — it currently fires only on spec.permission === 'admin'. If new super_admin ops add their own permission level without updating this predicate, super_admin cookie sessions skip the 30-min idle check at the API while still being held to it at the page layer (requireSuperAdmin -> adminSessionIsStale). The fix is widening the predicate to spec.permission !== 'user' so any non-user gate also enforces freshness. Test it: a super_admin op should call enforceAdminFreshness on source:'web'.

When stripping a field from a .strict() Zod schema that's already used by service-layer code, the validator change cascades immediately: the service can't construct payloads with the removed field anymore. Bundle the service-side cleanup into the same commit as the schema change — splitting them leaves the build red between commits and breaks the 'each task leaves the codebase green' invariant.

When moving an app-router page (e.g. /admin/categories/page.tsx → /admin/settings/categories/page.tsx) that imports a sibling component via relative path (../_components/page-header), the relative import depth needs to bump from ../ to ../../ in lockstep. tsc catches this immediately, but easy to miss in the diff because the page content is otherwise unchanged. Sweep with: grep -rn 'from "\.\./_components' on the moved subtree before the typecheck.

Long-running Next.js dev server can hold a stale Drizzle metadata state after a schema migration applies — even though the migration ran cleanly. Symptom: every route 500s until the dev server is hard-restarted. Saw this on 2026-06-15 after migration 0025 added membership_plan.tier.

When a feature flag-style runtime knob only feeds one screen and changes rarely, the MLabs answer is to push it into packages/config/src/brand.ts (the rebrand layer), not to keep it as an app_setting row. Brand.ts is the canonical place forks edit on rebrand. Reserve app_setting rows for things that genuinely change at runtime (e.g. reminder_schedule's cron windows) — anything that's effectively brand copy gets compiled in. Test: if you can imagine the value changing 0-1 times in the lifetime of a fork, hardcode it in brand.ts.

Hand-authored data-only Drizzle migrations follow a 3-file pattern in this repo: (1) the .sql file with pure SQL (DELETE/INSERT) and a header comment, (2) an appended entry in meta/_journal.json with the same shape as siblings (idx, version, when, tag, breakpoints), (3) a snapshot file copied forward verbatim from the previous step (since schema didn't change). Established by 0022_seed_reminder_schedule.sql. Drizzle-kit doesn't generate these — you write them. The migration runner already advisory-locks (pg_advisory_xact_lock per ADR 0008), so safe under parallel deploys.

Pure SQL hand-authored Drizzle migrations need the journal entry to be written BEFORE running pnpm db:migrate — the migrator reads from _journal.json to know what to apply. If you create the .sql file but don't add the journal entry, db:migrate succeeds without doing anything because it only sees the journal-listed migrations. After adding the entry, re-run db:migrate and verify with a SELECT that the data change actually landed.

Server-side days_remaining is now a convention across the admin renewals surface (renewals queue + admin businesses list + business-subscriptions queries). Always precompute Math.ceil((end_date - now) / DAY_MS) in the service/op handler — not the client component — to dodge the RSC hydration drift that suppressHydrationWarning was added to paper over in 2026-06-14.

When extending an existing admin surface with a date/expiry helper, check apps/web/src/features/admin/renewals/ first — expiryLabel (today/tomorrow/in Nd/OVERDUE Nd/MM/DD/YYYY) is the established dialect across the admin shell. Extract + share rather than introducing a second wording.

Pre-commit lefthook in this repo runs check-migrations, check-no-server-actions, check-contrast, and check-mobile-tailwind — NOT lint. So pre-existing unused-import warnings and process.env-direct-access errors stay invisible at commit time. If a task touches a file with pre-existing lint warnings, they don't block your commit but they DO show up in /mlabs-qa or CI later.

Playwright URL-only navigation assertions (toHaveURL) silently pass even if the destination renders an error boundary. ALWAYS pair toHaveURL with at least one assertion about destination content (a heading, a known body element) and capture a screenshot of the destination — otherwise 'the link works' verifies routing but not rendering.

When a feature has a hardcoded TS const AND a DB-backed dynamic catalog for the same concept (e.g. VALID_CATEGORIES + category table), the hardcoded const is the source-of-truth for the form picker but the DB drives every read surface. They drift silently because there's no FK; a rename in admin orphans every business already using the old slug. Always check for this pattern when reviewing admin CMS-style features — the form should fetch options from the same source the rest of the app reads.

Before assuming an ApiError factory exists, check packages/api/src/errors.ts. Only six static factories are defined: unauthorized | idleTimeout | forbidden | notFound | badRequest | internal. No .conflict(), .ratelimited(), etc. The codebase routes 409-style cases through badRequest with a domain-specific code (categories.x, businesses.x) carrying the semantics.

Drizzle-kit snapshot chain breaks if any two snapshots share the same top-level id/prevId. This happens when someone copies a snapshot verbatim for a data-only migration (the pattern documented in 0022/0026 commit messages). The migrations still apply via journal, but db:generate refuses to run. Fix: each new snapshot must have a fresh id (crypto.randomUUID()) and prevId = previous snapshot's id. Pre-existing 0025/0026 collision in this repo blocks db:generate until repaired.

Community board rebrand (Post on AIRA): when the user's wedge shifts from 'asks' to 'classifieds,' the cheap path is copy + two nullable contact columns + interest-button rename. Resist adding a post_type enum on the first pass — it explodes scope into admin filters, per-type copy, and migration. Re-evaluate once real posting behaviour reveals genuine clusters.

community.post_edited audit-meta union (packages/validators/src/audit-meta.ts) caps the editable-field set — any new admin-editable column on community_post must widen the union AND add a per-field before/after pair, else editing the column either fails the audit type-check or silently escapes the trail.

Zod 4 convention in this repo: email validators use z.email(message), NOT z.string().email(). See packages/validators/src/auth.ts:17. A plan that proposes Zod 3 syntax will type-check (alias) but breaks the in-repo idiom.

tel:/mailto: hrefs in this repo: pass raw validated values, never encodeURIComponent — React already escapes attribute values, and over-encoding mangles real phone numbers (+1 (404) 555-1212 -> %2B1%20%28404%29...) that dialers reject. Server-side validation (max length + Zod email) is the safety net.

Rebrand/copy-change plans must check the no-brand-string-literal ESLint rule up front. Any literal that says the brand name ("AIRA", "Million Labs") will fail lint even when correct copy-wise; design labels around brand.name from @aira/config from the start so the verification pass doesn't have to repair a Task.

Drizzle snapshot chain corruption surfaces only at db:generate time, not at db:migrate. If two meta/<n>_snapshot.json files share an id, all subsequent generate calls fail with a 'collision' error; fix is a fresh UUID for the duplicate + matching prevId on the next snapshot. Pure metadata, no SQL change. Always check the chain before adding columns if recent migration commits look unusual.

Community boards with mixed 'asks' + 'classifieds': commenting wants thread-style (parent_id self-FK, 1-level cap), interest stays as the lightweight 'this resonates' signal. Don't conflate them — the interest count is the public social signal, comments are the discussion. They route to different notification kinds and have different moderation models (interest = no moderation; comments = post-moderation).

Author edits an already-approved community post → revert status to pending and clear approved_at/expires_at. Prevents bait-and-switch (post benign content → get approved → edit to spam) without locking edits entirely. The audit trail captures both the field changes AND the status transition. Same pattern applies to any moderation-gated entity that allows author edits.

Notification body union has three coordinated touchpoints in this monorepo: packages/db/src/types.ts (canonical, used by jsonb column $type<>()), packages/validators/src/notifications.ts (over-the-wire Zod schema), and apps/web/src/features/notifications/components/notification-item.tsx (renderer). A stale duplicate exists at apps/web/src/features/notifications/types.ts — currently unused, but plans naming it as 'the' file are incorrect.

Postgres CHECK constraints can't contain subqueries, so an N-level reply cap (parent's parent_id IS NULL) can't be enforced as a CHECK — needs a BEFORE-INSERT trigger or service-layer guard. For MVPs, service-layer + Vitest cover is the cheaper pick; matches how other invariants like the 1-active-post limit are enforced.

Next 16 dynamic route adapter merges path params into the parsed input by name. Schemas must use the same field name as the route segment (e.g. `/posts/[id]/comments` requires the schema to call the post id `id`, not `post_id`). Existing convention across this monorepo: every dynamic-param schema field is named `id`.

ApiError.forbidden(message) hard-codes the code to `auth.forbidden`. For domain-specific 403 codes (`community.forbidden`, `businesses.forbidden`, etc.), use the constructor: new ApiError({ status: 403, code: 'domain.forbidden', message }).

Adding a new NotificationBody variant requires touching FOUR files coordinated: packages/db/src/types.ts (canonical union), packages/validators/src/notifications.ts (over-the-wire Zod), apps/web/src/features/notifications/components/notification-item.tsx (web renderer), AND apps/mobile/app/(app)/notifications.tsx (mobile's exhaustiveness-checked switch). Forgetting the mobile one fails @aira/mobile typecheck.

When a PRD spec'd both a denormalised 'is_X' boolean flag on user AND the underlying FK that the flag would derive from (e.g. is_business_contact + Business.owner_user), prefer the FK alone. The 'EXISTS (rel WHERE fk = user.id)' query is the source of truth; the boolean would need trigger maintenance to stay correct, and the targeting query that needs the segment can scan the FK index directly. Applies any time a PRD shows both — the flag is usually a Bubble-shaped concession.

When an existing op's output schema is shared by both admin and public endpoints (e.g. BusinessSchema in @aira/validators/businesses), and a new field is admin-only (e.g. joined owner record), the convention is to add the FK alone to the public schema (opaque, no PII) and put the joined object as a SEPARATE field on the admin-detail op output. Avoid inventing a new admin-only base schema — every existing admin extension follows AdminBusinessItemSchema = BusinessSchema.extend({...}). Inventing a parallel base would diverge from the established pattern.

Auditability beats noise: an empty fan-out (e.g. broadcast with 0 recipients) should still write a single audit row with recipient_count: 0 rather than skipping the audit. Admins benefit from a record of every attempt, including no-ops, when reviewing 'why didn't this go out?'. The cost is one extra row per zero-recipient broadcast — negligible.

When a service function needs brand-interpolated strings (e.g. "An admin at ${brand.name}…") for a notification body, do NOT import @aira/config inside the service. Pass the pre-composed strings as args from the op layer instead. Keeps @aira/services framework-agnostic and matches how messages.service.sendMessage already handles email content composition.

apps/web's apiClient interface doesn't expose a put() method — only get/post/patch/delete. Admin mutating endpoints in this codebase all use POST regardless of REST verb purity. If you wire a route handler as 'export const PUT = ...' you'll have no clean way to call it from the apiClient. Stick with POST for writes.

Adding a required (non-optional) field to BusinessSchema immediately breaks @aira/services typecheck because the toBusiness mapper in packages/services/src/businesses/queries.ts must project every BusinessSchema field. The marketing preview mock PREVIEW_BUSINESS in apps/web/src/components/marketing/business-panel.tsx also needs the new field. Plan these two updates as part of the validator-edit task so the schema task leaves the codebase compiling.

/admin/businesses/[id] requires super_admin role (not just admin) because the detail page calls listCitiesAdminOp via apiServerFetch to populate the city dropdown, and that op is restricted to super_admin. A plain admin can't load the detail page at all — pre-existing constraint, not part of any specific feature. Any QA setup that needs to drive the admin business detail page must seed a super_admin persona.

Better Auth's databaseHooks (user.create.after, etc.) fire only when signups go through Better Auth's API. Direct drizzle writes to the user table BYPASS them — useful for seed scripts that need deterministic role assignment, dangerous if you expected the bootstrap hook to promote your seeded admin. Either path works; just be aware of which one you're on.

Better Auth's account table in this repo (packages/db/src/schema/auth.ts) has NO unique constraint on (account_id, provider_id) — only a PK on id and an index on userId. Any upsert that tries ON CONFLICT (account_id, provider_id) will fail at runtime. Either use the PK (deterministic account.id per seeded persona, then ON CONFLICT (id)) or add a UNIQUE INDEX via migration. Don't assume BA's natural key is enforced just because the column exists.

When a packages/db/scripts/ Node tool needs to import from a package that isn't in @aira/db's package.json (e.g. better-auth/crypto), it still resolves at runtime + typecheck because this repo's .npmrc has node-linker=hoisted + shamefully-hoist=true + public-hoist-pattern[]=*. All workspace deps are flat in the root node_modules. No need to add the dep to @aira/db's package.json just to use it from a script.

updateBusinessOp doesn't audit field-level diffs — only archive/restore/owner-assign actions write to audit_log. When a plan says 'reuse existing business-update audit' for a new column, confirm whether per-field audit infra exists first; otherwise the choice is targeted-audit (per-field) vs generic-audit (diff-all-fields), and the cost looks different.

BusinessSchema is plain z.object() (not .strict()), so Zod safeParse silently strips unknown keys. Any 'parse the public response to detect leakage' acceptance criterion is a no-op — the test always passes whether or not the field leaks. Verify public-API leakage with raw-body JSON inspection instead, OR add .strict() as a separate refactor.

Single toBusiness mapper in packages/services/src/businesses/queries.ts is shared by every read path. Adding an admin-only column is NOT a one-line addition — it requires either forking the mapper (toBusiness + toBusinessAdmin) or threading a flag, plus a parallel attachRelations helper. Don't mistake 'add a column' for 'add a line' when reviewing future plans that touch this surface.

Adding a new AuditMeta.kind requires four coordinated edits (union + KNOWN_AUDIT_ACTIONS + render-detail.tsx switch + AUDIT_ACTION_LABEL_OVERRIDES). The _ActionsCoverage compile-check catches union/array drift but NOT the render-detail switch — that surfaces via 'never' default branch hitting tsc. Always enumerate all four when planning a new audit kind.

When the migration tool returns 'Command db:generate not found', the actual workspace script is 'generate' (not 'db:generate') and lives in packages/db. The CLAUDE.md uses 'pnpm db:generate' which is wrong — use 'pnpm --filter @aira/db generate' from the root. Set DATABASE_URL even for generate (the script reads it via process.env even when it doesn't need to connect).

Splitting a Zod schema into public + admin variants (BusinessSchema vs BusinessAdminSchema) is cheap at the type layer but requires forking the row mapper too — TypeScript widening (BusinessAdmin extends Business) is assignable upward but won't make the field appear at runtime unless the mapper projects it. The fork pattern: keep toBusiness as-is, add a toBusinessAdmin that spreads it + appends the extra fields, plus a sibling attachRelationsHelper. Same call sites get to choose which to use.

getCategoryTree passes includeInactive: true to getCategoriesByCity — public sidebar and any other tree consumer see inactive rows. Filter at the consumer if you want active-only; the tree op itself does NOT filter. Same gotcha will show up any time someone reaches for the tree op expecting it to be 'active only'.

Double-click as a remove gesture is intuitive to engineers (dblclick fires after click) but discoverability-hostile to users — they don't know to try it, and on touch it conflicts with browser double-tap-to-zoom. Standard pattern across Pinterest/Spotify/Apple/etc is single-click toggle with the icon state telegraphing direction. When a user requests double-click-to-remove, default to recommending the toggle with their concern addressed (e.g. accidental clicks bounce against an idempotent backend, not a confusing gesture).

The codebase already uses HTTP verbs cleanly — DELETE / PATCH / POST appear in route handlers (community interests, profile, avatar, admin sponsorship cancel, image delete). When planning a new REST endpoint, don't default to POST-everything; verb alignment is the project convention. The api-client (createApiClient) supports verb methods directly via apiClient.post/delete/etc.

Idempotency direction is a per-feature semantic call, not a global pattern. community.post_interest throws on duplicate add because the post author needs the audit trail; business favorites are fully idempotent (silent on duplicate) because they're personal preferences with no second party. When following a 'precedent' table like post_interest for a new join entity, verify the semantic match — same table shape doesn't mean same error semantics.

Zod 4's forward inference from input: ZodType<I> to handler input: I doesn't fire when the handler uses input only for property access (no back-inference from a service signature that expects the full type). Symptom: 'input is of type unknown' on input.someProp. Fix: explicit type annotation on the handler arg via z.infer<typeof Schema>. The community ops avoid this by passing input straight to the service which itself takes the full type — that back-infers; primitive-arg services don't.

When adding a new module to @aira/validators (e.g. ./favorites), update both src/index.ts (for the barrel) AND package.json exports map (for subpath imports). Subpath imports like @aira/validators/favorites will silently fail with 'cannot find module' until the exports map entry exists.

apiClient.post/patch signatures are (path, body, init?) — body is the SECOND POSITIONAL argument, NOT { body } inside init. Wrong: apiClient.post(url, { body: { x: 1 } }) sends {"body":{"x":1}} as the request body and Zod strict schemas reject it as a 400. Right: apiClient.post(url, { x: 1 }). DELETE is (path, init?) with no body arg. Mis-copying { body: ... } from fetch's options shape is the failure mode.

EAS init produces a two-stage dependency that's easy to miss in plans: the Apple Team ID surfaces in App Store Connect ONLY after the dev team is enrolled + the app record is created, and the Android signing-key SHA-256 surfaces in Play Console ONLY after at least one AAB is uploaded to a track. Both feed the .well-known files. Plans should split init (Step 1, produces values) from value-propagation into the repo (Step 2, commits real Team ID + SHA-256 into the route handlers). One task makes the dependency invisible.

apps/web/public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association has the {{APPLE_TEAM_ID}} placeholder in TWO places (applinks.details[0].appID AND webcredentials.apps[0]). Substitution tasks that mention 'replace the Team ID placeholder' often miss the webcredentials site, breaking Apple's password-autofill domain hint without breaking applinks. Plans must enumerate both sites explicitly; a grep for {{ in apps/web/public/.well-known/ post-substitution catches half-finished work.

Plans that mix code-writeable tasks with CLI/portal-only operations need explicit [CODE] vs [HUMAN] tagging in the review's implementation plan, plus Pause-if triggers that resume on user-quoted output values (projectId, Team ID, SHA-256). Otherwise /mlabs-code either guesses (bad) or pauses indefinitely on every task (slow). The pattern: HUMAN tasks pause + echo the exact CLI command + expected output; CODE tasks pick up the value the user pastes back.

EAS Update OTA configuration has an implicit chicken-egg: app.config.ts needs updates.url = 'https://u.expo.dev/<projectId>' but the projectId only exists after 'eas init' runs. Plans that list 'edit app.config.ts to add updates.url' as a single task can't actually be executed by /mlabs-code without splitting around the eas init human-step. Fix: use 'eas update:configure' AFTER init — it writes the URL with the right projectId automatically. Don't hand-write the URL.

Forks of this template carry BOTH the FORK_CHECKLIST.md.template (lives forever as a template for next forks) AND a derived FORK_CHECKLIST.md (the actual fork's living checklist). When ticking items as part of a S0 ship, update the DERIVED file, not the template. Also: the template's checklist items can go stale — bundle ID / package items in the AIRA fork's well-known files were substituted live in 2026-06-09, so those template lines are misleading for the AIRA fork.

EAS Build schema: at the profile top level, autoIncrement is a BOOLEAN (true/false). The string forms ('buildNumber' / 'versionCode') are only valid on the per-platform nested config (build.<profile>.ios.autoIncrement: 'buildNumber'). Setting 'autoIncrement: "buildNumber"' at the profile level fails immediately at eas init with 'must be a boolean'. The Expo docs sometimes use the string form in examples without specifying which level — always check whether the example nests it inside ios/android or sets it at the profile root.

eas init against a dynamic Expo config (app.config.ts function-form) prints 'Cannot automatically write to dynamic config' + exits with 'Error: project:init command failed' — but the project IS created on Expo's side. The exit code is misleading; the project exists at the printed URL. Manually add { extra: { eas: { projectId: '<uuid>' } } } to app.config.ts. Subsequent eas commands work normally.

Expo Go covers the same wiring-validation surface as a simulator-only EAS build (JS bundle compiles, imports resolve, screens render). When the user has Expo Go testing in their workflow already, the [dev/simulator] EAS build profile is redundant for proving the build pipeline — preview/production builds exercise the native side anyway. Worth offering 'skip simulator if you've already exercised the bundle in Expo Go' as a fast-path option.

EAS Build's tarball compressor caches binaries (notably React Native DevTools) under /tmp/runner/eas-cli-nodejs/<uuid>-shallow-clone/.cache/dotslash/... and on cleanup runs rmdir. On Replit the /tmp/runner/* path has permissions that block the rmdir, so the build fails with 'EACCES: permission denied, rmdir' before ever reaching EAS Build compute (no billing impact). Fix: 'rm -rf /tmp/runner/eas-cli-nodejs' (may need chmod -R u+w first) then retry. Symptom-only — the EAS-side state (channel, branch, keystore generation) persists across the failed attempt.

When a third-party CLI you can't modify (eas-cli, npm, expo) fails with EACCES on rmdir of its own cache files, you can't apply the try/catch + log-and-continue pattern you'd use in your own code. Two equivalent mechanisms: (1) .easignore / .dockerignore / equivalent skip-list to prevent the path from being included in the tool's scope — declarative version of 'don't fight it'; (2) TMPDIR override to relocate the work to a path your user owns where chmod isn't needed. Underlying principle is the same: best-effort cleanup shouldn't abort the real work. Mechanism differs based on whether you own the code.

When a feature has heavy upstream-already-shipped context (like F21 inheriting all of G1's owner-targeting plumbing), the plan should call out 'don't re-litigate these' explicitly in the Problem section. Otherwise the reviewer ends up asking about decisions that were already locked elsewhere (e.g. why isn't there owner identity work? — because G1 shipped it). Naming the shipped upstream pieces upfront prevents 'I thought we needed to design X' confusion at /mlabs-review time.

Plans that propose a new API namespace (e.g. /api/v1/me/*) when an existing namespace covers the same conceptual scope (e.g. /api/v1/profile/*) should be flipped at review. Parallel namespaces for 'current user's resources' are an unnecessary cognitive split. Check the codebase's existing /api/v1/* surface before approving a new top-level path segment.

Synchronous fan-out endpoints over an external HTTP service (Expo Push, Stripe, etc.) need a server-side timeout cap with partial-success reporting. Without it: admin UI hangs for the platform's default fetch timeout (~2min) on a vendor outage. 60s AbortController + structured partial-state output is the documented pattern. Tighter caps lose partial visibility; no cap risks user-perceived hangs.

F21 by_categories audience: joined through business_category N:M (not the legacy businesses.category text column the review T4 SQL sample hinted at). The admin modal's category picker draws from listCategoriesTreeOp which returns categories.id values; the legacy column would need a name→id map admins don't have. Locked as deliberate deviation in T4 commit + roadmap decision log.

User preference for Expo SDK choice: stay on the SDK Expo Go ships, not the latest. Iteration speed via the public Expo Go (scan-the-QR loop) is more valuable than being on the bleeding edge with a custom Dev Client. Default to the Expo Go-shipping SDK for new forks; downgrade rather than build a Dev Client when a fork hits the version-mismatch wall. Locked 2026-06-23 with the SDK 55 → 54 downgrade plan.

F21 T12 mistake: pinned expo-notifications ~0.32.13 manually instead of letting Expo's resolver choose. SDK 55's bundledNativeModules.json wants ~55.0.22 (the version-aligned release where expo-* packages adopt the SDK major as their major). pnpm happily resolved to 0.32.17 (pre-alignment release line) and F21 code works there, but it was never the version SDK 55 intended. Locked policy going forward: never hand-pick an expo-* version; always run 'expo install <pkg>' so the resolver picks the SDK-aligned release. Surfaced during the SDK 54 downgrade review on 2026-06-23.

SDK downgrade across an Expo monorepo: expo install --fix tightens @types/react to a strict tilde range (e.g. ~19.1.17). If web has UI deps with hard-pinned @types/react@^19.2 peer-deps (e.g. @base-ui/react), this conflicts cross-app and produces 'Two different types with this name exist' tsc errors. Fix: root pnpm.overrides forcing a single @types/react + @types/react-dom version workspace-wide. Locked during 2026-06-23 SDK 55 → 54 downgrade.

Delete-with-audit ops must mirror community.deletePost: service pre-fetches snapshot for audit meta, throws 404 if absent, then runs audit + delete in a single db.transaction() so a failed audit rolls back the delete. Don't split audit and delete across op and service layers.

Adding a new audit action means three sync points, not two: AuditMeta union + KNOWN_AUDIT_ACTIONS (parity check is compile-time) + KNOWN_AUDIT_TARGET_TYPES if the action has a new target_type. The target_types array has no parity assertion, so it's the easy one to forget — without it the /admin/audit filter dropdown can't filter on the new target.

When a feature spans (audit-meta, validators, services, ops, page, components), the natural review-task order isn't always compile-safe. Order T1=audit-meta, T2=validators, T3=services, T4=ops+routes — then before committing T4, pull T8 (audit-log renderer) ahead so the AuditMeta exhaustiveness gate stays satisfied. Same trick for T5 page importing T6 tables: pull T6 ahead. Two reorderings preserved 'every commit compiles'.
